title: Count Number of Texts
summary: Alice texts Bob using a phone where digits map to letters.
statement: Alice texts Bob using a phone where digits map to letters. To input a letter, she presses the corresponding digit multiple times. For example, 's' requires four presses of '7', and 'k' requires two presses of '5'. Digits '0' and '1' are unused. Bob receives a string of pressed keys instead of the message. Given a string of pressed keys, calculate the number of possible messages Alice could have sent, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Digits two through six and eight have three letters; seven and nine have four.
A letter is encoded by one through that digit’s maximum consecutive equal presses.
Count all complete partitions of the received string and return the result modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: This is a partition-counting dynamic program over prefixes.
For each ending position, try equal-digit groups of lengths one through three or four.
Add dp[end-length] for each valid equal group, applying the modulus.
Every decoded message has one unique final press group, so the transitions partition all messages without overlap.
editorial: Every decoded message has one unique final press group, so the transitions partition all messages without overlap.

tests.explanation: The run 222 has four partitions and 33 has two, producing eight possible messages.
The four equal presses can be partitioned in eight valid ways when group size is at most four.
